rationale: unit:given.typing.declarations introduces Sigma and nominal classes, with given.classes/programs/syntax supplying names and finite-map/list notation. This unit introduces relative paths rho, their empty root and concatenation, signed entries, finite views A, types T, and base. Path and recursive classAt follow precisely those field sequences, including epsilon returning the starting class. ViewType.whole is the positive empty-path entry, not a distinct type constructor; the empty entry list is distinct from that root entry. Entry.valid excludes negative epsilon and checks declared paths; ViewType.WellFormed checks the declared root and all entries, and entriesDisjoint excludes equal as well as prefix-comparable paths irrespective of sign. Lean stores the authored set as a list, but these predicates and positive/negative observations do not distinguish list permutations. The inspected normalization context reconstructs canonical declaration-order lists before equality-sensitive uses, and normalization_entry_order checks this boundary. Positive subtrees, unknown omitted branches, and full versus partial information agree with the inspected observations definitions; raw malformed lists are outside the authored well-formed view domain.
limitations: General normalization correctness, including preservation of well-formedness/observations and idempotence, has not been supplied as a proved theorem; definitions are reviewed algorithmically on the authored well-formed domain.
